verdict.rationale: Inngest's own docs cover keyed concurrency limits, where a limit applies to each unique key value such as a user ID. That enables per-tenant caps. They also document function-level rate limiting as a hard cap on run starts within a time period, and the docs overview lists concurrency, throttling and rate limiting as managed capabilities. Missing for 10: explicit evidence that rate limits can be keyed per tenant (the rate-limit doc shows only function-level limits), documentation of fairness or anti-starvation behaviour across tenants, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I cap concurrency and set rate limits per workflow, per key, or per tenant so one hot customer can't starve the rest

citations.quote: Step concurrency can be optionally configured using "keys" which applies the limit to each unique value of the key (ex. user id).
Rate limiting is a hard limit on how many function runs can start within a time period.
We handle the backend infra, queueing, scaling, concurrency, throttling, rate limiting, and observability for you.
